the PSF values for beta beta-, beta + beta+ and E C E C DBD modes in nuclei of interest are now available in the literature, in a form suitable for use in the analysis of experimental data.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the phase-space factor for double-beta decay, which is an important ingredient in the theoretical prediction of the half-life.
a complete, accurate calculation of the phase space factor for the double beta decay modes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PSF values are now available in a very accurate and consistent way, for any nucleus and transition of interest.
, in the case of the beta-beta- decay, we provide PSF values with an accuracy of 0.5% or better for all nuclei and transitions.
we are able to predict the PSFs with a relative accuracy better than 0.5% for the allowed transitions and about 3% for the forbidden modes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PSF values for the beta+ beta+ mode are significantly smaller than those previously used, while the beta+EC and EC beta+ modes are significantly larger.
the PSF values should be re-calculated, using the improved methods and data, in all nuclei where DBD is observed, in order to have reliable predictions of the DBD rates and the neutrino parameters.
